tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,

# Backlog: where we lose score, and what to work on

As of 10 October 2026, 21:30. Source: the `tactical` run over the 10 hosted practice cases
(`20261010-211824-practice-tactical`, commit `96f7545`, mean 0.695), its trace and events, and the practice
leaderboard read at 21:35 (we are 5th of 22 with 73.2 points over our best scores; the leader has 79.0).

Every figure below is from that run unless a source is named. The "why" of each problem is read from the trace and
the `thread_hold` events; the rule in `tactical.py` behind each stop has not been traced line by line.

## 1. The cases by lever, with what the run lost

| Lever | Case | Score | EUR above C_best | Rounds used of 10 | How the thread ended |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price increase | P01 | 0.856 | 8,192 | 2 | held: "their offer meets our ask", supplier still `open` |
| Price increase (copper) | P02 | 0.686 | 14,854 | 2 | supplier `agreed` to our sheet |
| Raw-material surcharge | P08 | 0.570 | 75,422 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Raw-material surcharge | P18 | 0.419 | 42,133 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 5.00 → 5.25 → 5.50, its price |
| Renewal | P03 | 0.905 | 31,992 | 4 | held: "the supplier stopped moving" |
| Renewal | P04 | 0.860 | 324 | 3 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| RFQ | P05 | 0.742 | 21,153 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 30.46 → 28.00 against its 28.79 |
| Bundling | P07 | 0.721 | 25,607 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Capacity | P10 | 0.647 | 212,881 | 2 | `final_offer` in its first reply (33.80, alternative 31.90); we took the alternative |
| Quality | P11 | 0.545 | 43,244 | 4 | held: "last word: take it", supplier still `open` |

### The best any team reached, per case

From the arena's live page (screenshot of 10 October, about 21:05; 24 teams) against our best score per case
(`runs.md`, after P-14):

| Case | Lever | Best team | House agent | Teams that beat the house | Our best | Gap to the best |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P08 | raw-material surcharge | 0.91 | 0.75 | 1 | 0.603 | 0.31 |
| P18 | raw-material surcharge | 0.68 | 0.39 | 17 | 0.467 | 0.21 |
| P02 | price increase (copper) | 0.85 | 0.74 | 1 | 0.686 | 0.16 |
| P11 | quality | 0.81 | 0.31 | 17 | 0.692 | 0.12 |
| P05 | RFQ | 0.92 | 0.56 | 12 | 0.824 | 0.10 |
| P07 | bundling | 0.81 | 0.78 | 1 | 0.721 | 0.09 |
| P01 | price increase | 0.99 | 0.97 | 2 | 0.917 | 0.07 |
| P10 | capacity | 0.70 | 0.69 | 3 | 0.647 | 0.05 |
| P03 | renewal | 0.94 | 0.92 | 1 | 0.905 | 0.04 |
| P04 | renewal | 0.87 | 0.86 | 14 | 0.860 | 0.01 |

The two raw-material cases hold 0.52 of the 1.16 between us and the best team on every case; P08 at 0.91 was reached
by one team. The practice board showed us 6th with a mean of 0.73; the leader had 0.81.

## 2. The problems, largest first

### 2.1 We stop after two to four of ten rounds

No thread used more than four rounds. In P18 and P05 the supplier agreed to our own rising offer (P18: 5.00 → 5.25
→ 5.50 against its 5.60); in P01 and P11 the thread was held while the supplier's status was still `open`.

- P18: deal 264,784, our upper bound 259,433, C_best 222,651.
- P10 is a different case: the supplier called its first reply final (33.80, with an alternative at 31.90) and we
  took the alternative. The deal costs 1,541,808 against our upper bound of 1,374,881 and C_best 1,328,927; what
  would have moved it is not in the trace.
- P02 closed in round 2 below our own ask (358.45 against 361.34), after we offered an index clause.

### 2.2 Our estimate of what is reachable is too high in leverage cases

The upper bound (`plan` event) against the arena's C_best:

| Case | Upper bound | C_best | Upper bound above C_best |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | 272,392 | 223,424 | 21.9 % |
| P18 | 259,433 | 222,651 | 16.5 % |
| P08 | 1,028,315 | 960,309 | 7.1 % |
| P07 | 319,069 | 299,241 | 6.6 % |
| P03 | 4,102,637 | 3,909,043 | 5.0 % |
| P01 | 1,143,596 | 1,096,816 | 4.3 % |
| P10 | 1,374,881 | 1,328,927 | 3.5 % |
| P04 | 197,524 | 196,529 | 0.5 % |
| P02 | 2,282,867 | 2,235,514 | 2.1 % |
| P11 | 710,733 | 722,500 | -1.6 % |

An offer inside a bound that is too high counts as good enough, so the thread closes early (2.1).

### 2.3 A lever the supplier names is not pulled

P11: the supplier wrote "Faster payment would help us more than anything" in four replies, and "If you want a lower
price, we need to drop the chargebacks". The profile had it as `cash_short`. Its price went 47.00 → 48.50 → 47.00 →
46.50 → 46.50 and we took it with six rounds left. P07: "A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the
price" in round 4.

### 2.4 Arguments that are spent for nothing

- The price-history argument came back "it holds, but it does not change our calculation" in five cases (P18, P08,
  P10, P02, P11). It takes one of the three argument slots of the first e-mail each time.
- P07: the forecast was cited in four e-mails; three came back `duplicate`, and the supplier answered "that volume
  change was already factored into our previous calculation" three times.

### 2.5 What is no longer a problem: the volume question

On 10 October in the afternoon the most common supplier sentence was "Which volume can you commit to?", unanswered
(`rejections.md`, row 1). In this run the forecast argument came back "it holds and we took it into account" in P18,
P08, P02, P07 and P11.

### 2.6 A final offer is final on practice

`playbook`'s closing offer after a final offer made three suppliers walk away (P04, P07, P18):
[`benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md`](benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md). Problem 2.1 is about the rounds
before a final offer, not about pushing past one.

### 2.7 Our cost of a deal misses the relationship charge

P02 (`stabilise`), run `20261010-221425-practice-tactical-slow25`: we accepted EUR 345.39 and computed C as 2,135,441.
The arena's C is 2,314,646, of which 179,204 is the relationship charge for leaving the supplier below its
sustainable margin; the deal is above C_open and scored 0. At 358.45 (run `20261010-211824-practice-tactical`) the
charge was 56,127. Our estimate of the charge was 0 in both, so the guard that refuses a deal worse than the opening
did not fire.

## 3. Work items

| # | Item | Cases it concerns | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~~Concede more slowly while the supplier is `open`~~ - tried as `tactical-slow25`: sandbox D02 0.587 → 0.671, practice mean 0.695 → 0.621 (0.696 → 0.690 without P02). No gain. | P18, P05 | 2.1 |
| 2 | Do not hold a thread on "last word" or "meets our ask" while the status is `open` and the supplier names a lever | P11, P01 | 2.1, 2.3 |
| 3 | Lower the upper bound for leverage cases, or stop using it as a reason to close | P05, P18, P08, P07 | 2.2 |
| 4 | When a supplier names a lever twice, send a sheet that gives it (shortest payment, no chargeback) at its price | P11, P07 | 2.3 |
| 5 | Drop the price-history argument from the first e-mail; never cite one ID twice | all | 2.4 |
| 6 | ~~In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, estimate the supplier's cost before pushing the price down, and stop where the relationship charge outweighs the price~~ - done, see 3a | P02, P01, P03, P10 | 2.7 |

## 3a. Done tasks (10-11 October, runs.md P-16 to P-27)

State after it: `tactical` on `6bb73d1`, full pass `20261011-010356-practice-tactical`, mean 0.746, 10 of 10 deals
(0.695 in the run this backlog was written from).

| new | first ask at most 13 % under the quote for a `routine` goal | P07 0.663 → 0.740 |
| new | brief reading: `C_open` when no opening keeps the must-haves (P10, P11), must-haves read on the supplier's standard terms in the send guard, null `parts` / `round_limit`; `tests/test_brief_variants.py` runs the planning step on 100 changed copies of the recorded cases | 241 tests pass, 8 expected failures on briefs outside the API description |
| tried, dropped | complaints as further quality arguments (P11: `duplicate`); the contract's index clause against the supplier's index argument (P08, P18: not read as an argument); first ask at the cost minimum with the 0.4 % of C step (P02 0.421) | [`TRYED.md`](TRYED.md) |

## 3b. Todo (as of 11 October, 01:40)

In this order:

1. **Decide which commit plays the final.** `gameplan-2026-10-11.md` names the tag `final-candidate-2026-10-11`
   (`b3f06da`); main is now `9e64347` with the margin charge in C and other changed defaults.

# Run registry

Every run on the arena gets a row here: practice runs (they spend the team's quota) always, sandbox runs when they
inform a decision. Rules: [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#run-registry-and-pushed-code-only). Newest rows go at the bottom
of each table.

- **Commit:** the pushed commit the run used (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`).
- **Strategy:** `--strategy` value.
- **Parameters:** cases, `--llm`, flags, anything that changes behaviour.
- **Results:** per-case scores and the mean.
- **Conclusions:** what we learned and what changes because of it.

Scores are the arena's case score, 0-1. Sandbox cases are D01 (price increase, stabilise) and D02 (RFQ with two
suppliers, leverage).

**Reconstructed rows (before 10 Oct 2026, 18:30 UTC).** The registry was introduced after these runs:
- Commit and author were inferred from the session times, the commit times and the e-mail texts; the arena API does
  not record them. Inferred values are marked *likely*.
- My own sandbox runs used code that was committed later (hash shown as "uncommitted → hash").

content.content:
# What moves the arena's suppliers: our 293 practice sessions

As of 11 October 2026, about 01:30. Source: every ended practice session of our team key (293; P01-P18, all
strategies and commits since 10 October). They come from `negotiator session <sid>` (trace, claim checks, scores) and
`negotiator backoffice <sid>` (the supplier's internal notes after the case). Both are read-only calls that spend no
quota. The raw files sit in `agent/data/replays/` and `agent/data/backoffice/` (git-ignored). The analysis scripts
were one-off and are not in the repository.

These are correlations across our own sessions, so strategy versions are mixed. Where the back office states the
supplier's rule outright, that rule is direct evidence; everything else is a lead to test with one practice session
per case.

## 1. The supplier's rules, from its back office

| Note in the back office | Count | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| "The buyer shows a much lower rival quote. I give half the step now and check the rest." | 50 | P05 |
| "Checked: give the rest of the step." (the next round) | 47 | P05 |
| "The buyer wants more than my band allows (band ends at …, buyer at …). Approve a further step?" | 10 | P02, P03, P10 |
| "Approved: you may go further, within our rules." | 7 | P02, P03 |
| "My call: hold." | 135 | all but P10 |
| "My call: walk_away." | 7 | P01, P04, P05, P18 |

- **RFQ (P05).** A much lower rival quote buys a step in two halves: half now, the rest after the check, in the next
  reply, whatever we send.
  - Best P05 session (0.839, `2d73b8dc2cadc8c6`): we cited the rival's 31.5. Dralveck went 36 → 29.5, we asked 27.85
    and it agreed at 27.85 (the rest of the step).
  - A 0.742 session (`0a55ee9e09cf56d9`): same opening, Dralveck went 36 → 30.5. We then offered 28.79 on our own and
    it agreed at once, before it would have given the rest anyway.
- **Approval ladder (P02, P03, P10).** An ask beyond the manager's band goes to a committee, which approved a further
  step in 7 of the 10 cases we saw. We reached the band only 10 times in 293 sessions.

## 2. What the supplier says about our data

The most common sentences (numbers masked):

| Sentence | Count |
|---|---|
| "We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 184 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 104 |
| "Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data." | 90 |
| "We checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 80 |
| "We checked the rival quote data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 79 |
| "We see your figures, but we cannot give up margin right now. Faster payment would help us more than anything." | 54 |
| "We checked the quality record data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 48 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 40 |

Claim results: 905 verified, 35 duplicate, 4 contradicted.

### A duplicate is a series, not an ID

`api.md` says each ID counts once per case. On P08 (`../runs.md` P-33) a second fall of PPI-C2431 over a window
with IDs we had not cited (05 → 07, after 06 → 08 in round 1) came back `duplicate`: "it holds, but this kind of
fact was already taken into account in our previous calculation". One argument per index series per case.

### P08: what sets the price (31 sessions)

The supplier makes one big step in its first reply, then small ones, and calls its offer final in round 3. Its final
offer sat 0.04-0.18 under its first reply. The first reply depends on our first message:

| Our first message | Its first reply |
|---|---|
| PPI-C2431's fall + AS-14404's fall + order history | 5.41 (13 sessions) |
| order history + forecast, no PPI | 5.46 |
| AS-14404 alone, or with LCI-C | 5.57 |
| a delivery-record complaint (+ forecast) | 5.71 and 6.10 |

AS-14404 is answered "not our reality: covered at fixed prices until March 2027"; PPI-C2431 (36 % of its cost by our
cost drivers) is "taken into account"; a complaint raises the price. From round 3 we had nothing left to cite in
every session.

## 3. Our step against the supplier's next reply

Rounds 2 and later; "our step" is the change of our lowest ask against our previous ask to the same supplier.

| Our step | Replies | Supplier's mean drop | It held its price | Final offer | Agreed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no move | 65 | 0.60 % | 32 % | 25 % | 18 % |
| under 1 % | 245 | 0.59 % | 34 % | 31 % | 4 % |
| 1-3 % | 126 | 1.75 % | 12 % | 34 % | 13 % |
| over 3 % | 209 | 1.86 % | 12 % | 16 % | 34 % |

Steps under 1 % get a held price a third of the time; steps over 3 % get "agreed" a third of the time, which is the
supplier taking our concession.

## 4. The first message

The supplier's price drop in its first reply, compared within the same case and supplier (paired; the number of
suppliers where the difference is positive in brackets):

| First message | Difference in the first reply's drop |
|---|---|
| 2 or more cited arguments | +1.71 pp (8 of 12) |
| no cited argument | −2.52 pp (1 of 5) |
| first ask 15 % or more under the quote | +3.60 pp (5 of 9) |
| first ask under 8 % below the quote | −3.72 pp (4 of 9) |
| 2 or more questions | −2.39 pp (3 of 12) |
| a single term sheet | −2.24 pp (1 of 8) |
| a quality record cited | −2.18 pp (0 of 4) |
| a delivery record cited | −1.65 pp (4 of 12) |
| price history cited | +2.14 pp (6 of 8) |

Within each case, the session's score ranks with the first reply's drop at Spearman +0.63 (positive in 10 of 10
cases). It also ranks with the number of cited arguments (+0.55, 10 of 10), with "took it into account" replies (+0.47,
10 of 10) and with questions asked (−0.10; top third 0.6 questions per session, bottom third 2.2).

## 5. P08: the index clause

Offline with `arena_kit.total_cost` on the deal of `20261011-004458-practice-tactical` (P08, price 5.42, payment 90
days, 24 months):

| Index clause | C |
|---|---|
| none | 1,020,781 |
| deadband 5 % | 1,030,030 |
| deadband 3 % (the deal) | 1,039,278 |
| deadband 0 % | 1,053,152 |

The case expects AS-14404 to rise 6 % a year, so the clause we gave cost 18,497 against none: 0.105 of the score. The
supplier's final offer also held a 5 % deadband sheet at 5.46 (C 1,037,614), cheaper for us than the one we accepted.

## 6. Leads to test (one practice session per case each)

1. Steps of 1-3 % of C instead of 0.4 % crumbs, under 3 % so the supplier does not simply agree.
2. RFQ: cite a much lower rival offer to each bidder, then do not raise our ask in the next round - the rest of its
   step comes after its check. Cite a rival's new lower offer as soon as it appears (each offer has its own ID).

# What moves the arena's suppliers: our 293 practice sessions

As of 11 October 2026, about 01:30. Source: every ended practice session of our team key (293; P01-P18, all
strategies and commits since 10 October). They come from `negotiator session <sid>` (trace, claim checks, scores) and
`negotiator backoffice <sid>` (the supplier's internal notes after the case). Both are read-only calls that spend no
quota. The raw files sit in `agent/data/replays/` and `agent/data/backoffice/` (git-ignored). The analysis scripts
were one-off and are not in the repository.

These are correlations across our own sessions, so strategy versions are mixed. Where the back office states the
supplier's rule outright, that rule is direct evidence; everything else is a lead to test with one practice session
per case.

## 1. The supplier's rules, from its back office

| Note in the back office | Count | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| "The buyer shows a much lower rival quote. I give half the step now and check the rest." | 50 | P05 |
| "Checked: give the rest of the step." (the next round) | 47 | P05 |
| "The buyer wants more than my band allows (band ends at …, buyer at …). Approve a further step?" | 10 | P02, P03, P10 |
| "Approved: you may go further, within our rules." | 7 | P02, P03 |
| "My call: hold." | 135 | all but P10 |
| "My call: walk_away." | 7 | P01, P04, P05, P18 |

- **RFQ (P05).** A much lower rival quote buys a step in two halves: half now, the rest after the check, in the next
  reply, whatever we send.
  - Best P05 session (0.839, `2d73b8dc2cadc8c6`): we cited the rival's 31.5. Dralveck went 36 → 29.5, we asked 27.85
    and it agreed at 27.85 (the rest of the step).
  - A 0.742 session (`0a55ee9e09cf56d9`): same opening, Dralveck went 36 → 30.5. We then offered 28.79 on our own and
    it agreed at once, before it would have given the rest anyway.
- **Approval ladder (P02, P03, P10).** An ask beyond the manager's band goes to a committee, which approved a further
  step in 7 of the 10 cases we saw. We reached the band only 10 times in 293 sessions.

## 2. What the supplier says about our data

The most common sentences (numbers masked):

| Sentence | Count |
|---|---|
| "We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 184 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 104 |
| "Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data." | 90 |
| "We checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 80 |
| "We checked the rival quote data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 79 |
| "We see your figures, but we cannot give up margin right now. Faster payment would help us more than anything." | 54 |
| "We checked the quality record data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 48 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 40 |

Claim results: 905 verified, 35 duplicate, 4 contradicted.

### A duplicate is a series, not an ID

`api.md` says each ID counts once per case. On P08 (`../runs.md` P-33) a second fall of PPI-C2431 over a window
with IDs we had not cited (05 → 07, after 06 → 08 in round 1) came back `duplicate`: "it holds, but this kind of
fact was already taken into account in our previous calculation". One argument per index series per case.

### P08: what sets the price (31 sessions)

The supplier makes one big step in its first reply, then small ones, and calls its offer final in round 3. Its final
offer sat 0.04-0.18 under its first reply. The first reply depends on our first message:

| Our first message | Its first reply |
|---|---|
| PPI-C2431's fall + AS-14404's fall + order history | 5.41 (13 sessions) |
| order history + forecast, no PPI | 5.46 |
| AS-14404 alone, or with LCI-C | 5.57 |
| a delivery-record complaint (+ forecast) | 5.71 and 6.10 |

AS-14404 is answered "not our reality: covered at fixed prices until March 2027"; PPI-C2431 (36 % of its cost by our
cost drivers) is "taken into account"; a complaint raises the price. From round 3 we had nothing left to cite in
every session.

## 3. Our step against the supplier's next reply

Rounds 2 and later; "our step" is the change of our lowest ask against our previous ask to the same supplier.

| Our step | Replies | Supplier's mean drop | It held its price | Final offer | Agreed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no move | 65 | 0.60 % | 32 % | 25 % | 18 % |
| under 1 % | 245 | 0.59 % | 34 % | 31 % | 4 % |
| 1-3 % | 126 | 1.75 % | 12 % | 34 % | 13 % |
| over 3 % | 209 | 1.86 % | 12 % | 16 % | 34 % |

Steps under 1 % get a held price a third of the time; steps over 3 % get "agreed" a third of the time, which is the
supplier taking our concession.

## 4. The first message

The supplier's price drop in its first reply, compared within the same case and supplier (paired; the number of
suppliers where the difference is positive in brackets):

| First message | Difference in the first reply's drop |
|---|---|
| 2 or more cited arguments | +1.71 pp (8 of 12) |
| no cited argument | −2.52 pp (1 of 5) |
| first ask 15 % or more under the quote | +3.60 pp (5 of 9) |
| first ask under 8 % below the quote | −3.72 pp (4 of 9) |
| 2 or more questions | −2.39 pp (3 of 12) |
| a single term sheet | −2.24 pp (1 of 8) |
| a quality record cited | −2.18 pp (0 of 4) |
| a delivery record cited | −1.65 pp (4 of 12) |
| price history cited | +2.14 pp (6 of 8) |

Within each case, the session's score ranks with the first reply's drop at Spearman +0.63 (positive in 10 of 10
cases). It also ranks with the number of cited arguments (+0.55, 10 of 10), with "took it into account" replies (+0.47,
10 of 10) and with questions asked (−0.10; top third 0.6 questions per session, bottom third 2.2).

## 5. P08: the index clause

Offline with `arena_kit.total_cost` on the deal of `20261011-004458-practice-tactical` (P08, price 5.42, payment 90
days, 24 months):

| Index clause | C |
|---|---|
| none | 1,020,781 |
| deadband 5 % | 1,030,030 |
| deadband 3 % (the deal) | 1,039,278 |
| deadband 0 % | 1,053,152 |

The case expects AS-14404 to rise 6 % a year, so the clause we gave cost 18,497 against none: 0.105 of the score. The
supplier's final offer also held a 5 % deadband sheet at 5.46 (C 1,037,614), cheaper for us than the one we accepted.

## 6. Leads to test (one practice session per case each)

1. Steps of 1-3 % of C instead of 0.4 % crumbs, under 3 % so the supplier does not simply agree.
2. RFQ: cite a much lower rival offer to each bidder, then do not raise our ask in the next round - the rest of its
   step comes after its check. Cite a rival's new lower offer as soon as it appears (each offer has its own ID).
3. Raw material with a rising index: price the index clause in C and do not give it where it costs more than its
   price difference; offer payment or contract length instead.
4. First message: two or three verified arguments, no quality or delivery complaint outside quality cases, at most one
   question, a menu of options, a first ask at least 15 % under the quote outside strategic cases.
5. Approval-ladder cases: one ask beyond the supplier's band, so the committee is asked for a further step.

1	"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.
2	
3	C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
4	the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
5	needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
6	strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
7	too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
8	not in the language model.
9	"""
10	
11	import math
12	import operator
13	from datetime import date
14	
15	# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
16	RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
17	OPS = {
18	    "<=": operator.le,
19	    "<": operator.lt,
20	    ">=": operator.ge,
21	    ">": operator.gt,
22	    "==": operator.eq,
23	    "!=": operator.ne,
24	}
25	
26	
27	def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
28	    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
29	    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
30	    """
31	    b = case["buyer"]
32	    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
33	    plan = {
34	        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
35	        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
36	        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
37	        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
38	        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

content.content:
# Argument audit: what the arena can check and what we cite

As of 11 October 2026. A reading of files, no arena session and no strategy change.

Sources: `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md` ("What counts"), `negotiation-arena-kit/data/facts.json` (10,356 IDs),
and the sessions stored under `agent/runs/` on one machine: 102 practice sessions (P01-P18, 8 to 14 per case) and 98
sandbox sessions, 10 and 11 October, all strategies. The 293 replays behind [`bot-mechanics.md`](bot-mechanics.md) are
not on this machine; where a figure comes from that file it says so. The scripts were one-off and are not in the
repository. Strategy versions are mixed, so the counts are correlations.

## 1. What the arena checks

`api.md` lists six rows of checkable data; the trace (`interpreted.claims`) names the type it read from our e-mail.

| Arena type | We cite | Rule in `api.md` | Our kind in the code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index_change` | 2 × `idx`, one series | at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | `index`, `recent_drop` |
| `rival_quote` | the case's `quote` (its refs or our alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | once per supplier in an RFQ | `rival_offer`, `quote` |
| `delivery_record` | `sc` rows | mean on-time delivery | `scorecard` |
| `quality_record` | `sc` rows, also `qn` | mean ppm | `quality`, `complaint` |
| `price_history` | 2-8 × `po`, same part | each part is its own argument | `orders` |
| `volume_change` | `fc` | the recorded change | `forecast` |
| `should_cost` | `cost` | the estimate | `should_cost` |
| `notice_period` | a letter `doc` + the contract `ctr` | the letter's notice against the contract's | `notice` |
| (not seen in a trace) | `news` | "that it is about this supplier" | none |

At most three arguments are read per message. Each ID counts once per case; measured on P08 (`runs.md` P-33), one
index series counts once per case whatever the IDs. Meeting notes, suppliers and parts are context, not checks.

The order of the sentences in an e-mail: `ledger.arguments_read` reproduces the arena's reading of 1031 of 1033
replayed messages by ordering the arguments by kind, not by their place in the text (comment in `ledger.py`). The
local sessions hold no two first e-mails with the same arguments in a different order, so an effect of the order on
the price is not measured.

## 2. Coverage per case

Facts of each type that exist for the case's parts and suppliers, and how many of them any of our local sessions
cited. "Case quote" is the `quote` in the case's refs with its price against the supplier's opening.

| Case | `po` | `fc` | `cost` | `sc` | `qn` | `news` (topic) | Case quote | Drivers never cited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 15 | none | 143.22, opening 138.55 | none |
| P02 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 1 (374.95, above the quote) | 1 of 9 | 0 of 2 | none | 421.06, opening 370.96 | CU-NOTATION, PPI-C241 |
| P03 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 2 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 466.99, opening 438.21 | CU-NOTATION, PPI-C2611 |
| P04 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 10 | 0 of 1 (refocus) | 5.04, opening 4.96 | none |
| P05 | none | none | 0 of 1 (36.87) | 3 of 27 | none | 0 of 3 (renamed, free capacity, full order book) | none | none |
| P07 | 0 of 216 | 4 of 36 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 71 | none | none | PPI-C2594, LCI-C |
| P08 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 23 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 6.06, opening 6.05 | none |
| P10 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 22 | 0 of 1 (allocation) | none | PPI-C2219 |
| P11 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 1 of 16 | 0 of 1 (restructuring) | 53.56, opening 47.00 | PPI-C241 |
| P18 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 8 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 6.31, opening 6.10 | none |

Sandbox D01 and D02 keep their facts in the case, not in `facts.json`; D02's refs hold `quote:D02-ALT` (19.90, both
openings are lower: 16.00 and 17.10) and `news:N-0412`, neither cited in 48 sessions.

What the table shows:

- **`news` is the one checkable type we have never cited** - in no case and no session.
- **The case quote is never cited** because it is above the supplier's opening in all seven cases that have one;
  the code cites it only when it is lower (`baseline.py`).
- **The drivers never cited rose over twelve months.** Their only falls are over old or short windows (PPI-C241
  −4.0 % from 2024-11 to 2025-11, CU-NOTATION −2.2 % from 2026-01 to 2026-03, PPI-C2611 −1.1 %, PPI-C2594 −1.4 %;
  PPI-C2219 has none). `tactical+all_windows` cites those and was measured (`runs.md` P-36).
- `qn` complaints were measured on P11 and reverted (`TRYED.md`); `po` and `sc` are cited by their latest rows.

## 3. What a verified argument did

The supplier's sentence about each kind of data, counted over the local sessions (practice and sandbox):

| Data | "took it into account" | "a fair point" | "does not change our calculation" | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rival quote | 115 | 1 | 23 | - |
| should-cost | 11 | 1 | 0 | - |
| notice period | 13 | 2 | 0 | - |
| index change | 26 | 3 | 4 | 5 "cannot give up margin" (P11), 1 "not our reality" (P08), 3 "adjusted our price" (P11) |
| volume change | 32 | 5 | 10 (P04, P10) | 2 "cannot give up margin" (P11), 6 "price reductions frozen" (P03) |
| quality record | 24 | 10 | 1 | - |
| delivery record | 5 | 0 | 23 | - |
| price history | 0 | 0 | 52 | 6 "price reductions frozen" (P03) |

Claim results in the same sessions: 442 verified, 13 duplicate (12 of them forecasts, 1 a quality record), none
contradicted or irrelevant.

Price history was answered "does not change our calculation" in every one of 52 practice sessions, in eight cases.
`bot-mechanics.md` section 4 has the first reply's drop +2.14 pp where price history was cited (6 of 8 suppliers),
from the 293 replays; the two readings are not reconciled here.

The supplier's first reply by the arguments of our first e-mail, P08 (local sessions):

| First e-mail read as | First ask under the quote | First reply | Sessions |
|---|---|---|---|
| AS-14404, PPI-C2431, price history | 26-27 % | 5.41, 5.58 | 3 |
| price history, forecast | 19 % | 5.46 | 1 |
| AS-14404, LCI-C | 27 % | 5.57 | 1 |
| AS-14404 | 27 % | 5.57 | 1 |
| AS-14404, PPI-C2431 | 27 % | 5.59 | 1 |
| delivery record, forecast | 34 % | 5.71 | 1 |
| delivery record | 29 % | 6.10 | 1 |

## 4. P08: what is left to cite

Facts of a checkable type for `part:370010` and `sup:70710` that no local session cited:

| Fact | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| `news:20260822-24` | "at the trade fair" (topic: noise) | never cited |
| `quote:7200008` | the other supplier's 6.06 of 2026-09-09 | above the opening of 6.05 |
| `quote:7100065`, `quote:7100064`, `quote:7300008` | 5.41 (the other supplier, 2025-05-18), 5.34 and 5.45 (this supplier) | not in the case's refs; `api.md` checks the case's quote only |
| 23 × `qn`, 8 older `sc` rows | complaints, scorecards | a delivery record raised the first reply to 5.71 and 6.10 (section 3) |
| older windows of AS-14404 and PPI-C2431 | −8.1 % from 2024-11 to 2025-11 | one argument per series (`runs.md` P-33, P-36) |
| `ctr:4600070710#3.2` | the contract's own index clause | not read as an argument (`runs.md` P-24) |

Not checkable but in the data: the supplier's letter of 2026-07-06 (its alloy need is covered at fixed prices until
March 2027) and the call note of 2026-04-21 (its owner offered to walk us through the calculation). We asked for a
cost breakdown in nine local P08 sessions and received none; a breakdown file arrived on D02 only (43 of 86 asks).

The price the best team's score stands for, from `arena_kit.cost.total_cost` on the deal of
`20261011-010356-practice-tactical` (C_open 1,135,887, C_best 960,309; 90 days, 24 months):

| Score | C | Price, clause deadband 5 % | Price, no clause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.550 (ours, deadband 3 %) | 1,039,278 | 5.42 at deadband 3 % | - |
| 0.91 (best team, live page of 10 October) | 976,111 | 5.136 | 5.183 |
| 1.00 | 960,309 | 5.053 | 5.099 |

Our nine local P08 sessions: first replies 5.41 to 6.10, lowest supplier offer 5.38 (with a deadband of 0 %).
`bot-mechanics.md` (31 sessions): the final offer sat 0.04 to 0.18 under the first reply.

## 5. Where `news` exists

| Case | Supplier | News | Our argument without an ID today |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | sup:70250 | `news:20260309-03` advertises free machine capacity | `their_capacity`, after it writes "we have free capacity" (24 replies in 8 sessions) |
| P05 | sup:70240 | `news:20260710-18` fully booked into next year | - |
| P10 | sup:70410 | `news:20260822-23` allocates volumes | - |
| P11 | sup:70140 | `news:20260911-28` restructures with its banks | - |
| P04 | sup:70620 | `news:20260619-15` concentrates on larger accounts | - |
| D02 | - | `news:N-0412` (in the case's refs) | - |

Only P05's free-capacity item argues for a lower price; it is the one case in the hosted set where the type could
be cited to our advantage, and D02 is where it can be tried without quota.

## 6. Measured after the audit

`tactical+news` on sandbox D02 (`runs.md` S-37 to S-40, [record](benchmarks/2026-10-11-tactical-news-none.md)): the
arena reads the type `news`; cited to the bidder it is about it is `verified` and "taken into account" (D02 0.587 →
0.713, four of four runs), cited to the other bidder it is `irrelevant`. Not played on practice.

# Argument audit: what the arena can check and what we cite

As of 11 October 2026. A reading of files, no arena session and no strategy change.

Sources: `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md` ("What counts"), `negotiation-arena-kit/data/facts.json` (10,356 IDs),
and the sessions stored under `agent/runs/` on one machine: 102 practice sessions (P01-P18, 8 to 14 per case) and 98
sandbox sessions, 10 and 11 October, all strategies. The 293 replays behind [`bot-mechanics.md`](bot-mechanics.md) are
not on this machine; where a figure comes from that file it says so. The scripts were one-off and are not in the
repository. Strategy versions are mixed, so the counts are correlations.

## 1. What the arena checks

`api.md` lists six rows of checkable data; the trace (`interpreted.claims`) names the type it read from our e-mail.

| Arena type | We cite | Rule in `api.md` | Our kind in the code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index_change` | 2 × `idx`, one series | at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | `index`, `recent_drop` |
| `rival_quote` | the case's `quote` (its refs or our alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | once per supplier in an RFQ | `rival_offer`, `quote` |
| `delivery_record` | `sc` rows | mean on-time delivery | `scorecard` |
| `quality_record` | `sc` rows, also `qn` | mean ppm | `quality`, `complaint` |
| `price_history` | 2-8 × `po`, same part | each part is its own argument | `orders` |
| `volume_change` | `fc` | the recorded change | `forecast` |
| `should_cost` | `cost` | the estimate | `should_cost` |
| `notice_period` | a letter `doc` + the contract `ctr` | the letter's notice against the contract's | `notice` |
| (not seen in a trace) | `news` | "that it is about this supplier" | none |

At most three arguments are read per message. Each ID counts once per case; measured on P08 (`runs.md` P-33), one
index series counts once per case whatever the IDs. Meeting notes, suppliers and parts are context, not checks.

The order of the sentences in an e-mail: `ledger.arguments_read` reproduces the arena's reading of 1031 of 1033
replayed messages by ordering the arguments by kind, not by their place in the text (comment in `ledger.py`). The
local sessions hold no two first e-mails with the same arguments in a different order, so an effect of the order on
the price is not measured.

## 2. Coverage per case

Facts of each type that exist for the case's parts and suppliers, and how many of them any of our local sessions
cited. "Case quote" is the `quote` in the case's refs with its price against the supplier's opening.

| Case | `po` | `fc` | `cost` | `sc` | `qn` | `news` (topic) | Case quote | Drivers never cited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 15 | none | 143.22, opening 138.55 | none |
| P02 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 1 (374.95, above the quote) | 1 of 9 | 0 of 2 | none | 421.06, opening 370.96 | CU-NOTATION, PPI-C241 |
| P03 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 2 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 466.99, opening 438.21 | CU-NOTATION, PPI-C2611 |
| P04 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 10 | 0 of 1 (refocus) | 5.04, opening 4.96 | none |
| P05 | none | none | 0 of 1 (36.87) | 3 of 27 | none | 0 of 3 (renamed, free capacity, full order book) | none | none |
| P07 | 0 of 216 | 4 of 36 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 71 | none | none | PPI-C2594, LCI-C |
| P08 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 23 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 6.06, opening 6.05 | none |
| P10 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | 1 of 1 | 1 of 9 | 0 of 22 | 0 of 1 (allocation) | none | PPI-C2219 |
| P11 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 1 of 16 | 0 of 1 (restructuring) | 53.56, opening 47.00 | PPI-C241 |
| P18 | 3 of 72 | 1 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 | 0 of 8 | 0 of 1 (noise) | 6.31, opening 6.10 | none |

Sandbox D01 and D02 keep their facts in the case, not in `facts.json`; D02's refs hold `quote:D02-ALT` (19.90, both
openings are lower: 16.00 and 17.10) and `news:N-0412`, neither cited in 48 sessions.

What the table shows:

- **`news` is the one checkable type we have never cited** - in no case and no session.
- **The case quote is never cited** because it is above the supplier's opening in all seven cases that have one;
  the code cites it only when it is lower (`baseline.py`).
- **The drivers never cited rose over twelve months.** Their only falls are over old or short windows (PPI-C241
  −4.0 % from 2024-11 to 2025-11, CU-NOTATION −2.2 % from 2026-01 to 2026-03, PPI-C2611 −1.1 %, PPI-C2594 −1.4 %;
  PPI-C2219 has none). `tactical+all_windows` cites those and was measured (`runs.md` P-36).
- `qn` complaints were measured on P11 and reverted (`TRYED.md`); `po` and `sc` are cited by their latest rows.

## 3. What a verified argument did

The supplier's sentence about each kind of data, counted over the local sessions (practice and sandbox):

| Data | "took it into account" | "a fair point" | "does not change our calculation" | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rival quote | 115 | 1 | 23 | - |
| should-cost | 11 | 1 | 0 | - |
| notice period | 13 | 2 | 0 | - |
| index change | 26 | 3 | 4 | 5 "cannot give up margin" (P11), 1 "not our reality" (P08), 3 "adjusted our price" (P11) |
| volume change | 32 | 5 | 10 (P04, P10) | 2 "cannot give up margin" (P11), 6 "price reductions frozen" (P03) |
| quality record | 24 | 10 | 1 | - |
| delivery record | 5 | 0 | 23 | - |
| price history | 0 | 0 | 52 | 6 "price reductions frozen" (P03) |

Claim results in the same sessions: 442 verified, 13 duplicate (12 of them forecasts, 1 a quality record), none
contradicted or irrelevant.

Price history was answered "does not change our calculation" in every one of 52 practice sessions, in eight cases.
`bot-mechanics.md` section 4 has the first reply's drop +2.14 pp where price history was cited (6 of 8 suppliers),
from the 293 replays; the two readings are not reconciled here.

The supplier's first reply by the arguments of our first e-mail, P08 (local sessions):

| First e-mail read as | First ask under the quote | First reply | Sessions |
|---|---|---|---|
| AS-14404, PPI-C2431, price history | 26-27 % | 5.41, 5.58 | 3 |
| price history, forecast | 19 % | 5.46 | 1 |
| AS-14404, LCI-C | 27 % | 5.57 | 1 |
| AS-14404 | 27 % | 5.57 | 1 |
| AS-14404, PPI-C2431 | 27 % | 5.59 | 1 |
| delivery record, forecast | 34 % | 5.71 | 1 |
| delivery record | 29 % | 6.10 | 1 |

## 4. P08: what is left to cite

Facts of a checkable type for `part:370010` and `sup:70710` that no local session cited:

| Fact | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| `news:20260822-24` | "at the trade fair" (topic: noise) | never cited |
| `quote:7200008` | the other supplier's 6.06 of 2026-09-09 | above the opening of 6.05 |
| `quote:7100065`, `quote:7100064`, `quote:7300008` | 5.41 (the other supplier, 2025-05-18), 5.34 and 5.45 (this supplier) | not in the case's refs; `api.md` checks the case's quote only |
| 23 × `qn`, 8 older `sc` rows | complaints, scorecards | a delivery record raised the first reply to 5.71 and 6.10 (section 3) |
| older windows of AS-14404 and PPI-C2431 | −8.1 % from 2024-11 to 2025-11 | one argument per series (`runs.md` P-33, P-36) |
| `ctr:4600070710#3.2` | the contract's own index clause | not read as an argument (`runs.md` P-24) |

Not checkable but in the data: the supplier's letter of 2026-07-06 (its alloy need is covered at fixed prices until
March 2027) and the call note of 2026-04-21 (its owner offered to walk us through the calculation). We asked for a
cost breakdown in nine local P08 sessions and received none; a breakdown file arrived on D02 only (43 of 86 asks).

The price the best team's score stands for, from `arena_kit.cost.total_cost` on the deal of
`20261011-010356-practice-tactical` (C_open 1,135,887, C_best 960,309; 90 days, 24 months):

| Score | C | Price, clause deadband 5 % | Price, no clause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.550 (ours, deadband 3 %) | 1,039,278 | 5.42 at deadband 3 % | - |
| 0.91 (best team, live page of 10 October) | 976,111 | 5.136 | 5.183 |
| 1.00 | 960,309 | 5.053 | 5.099 |

Our nine local P08 sessions: first replies 5.41 to 6.10, lowest supplier offer 5.38 (with a deadband of 0 %).
`bot-mechanics.md` (31 sessions): the final offer sat 0.04 to 0.18 under the first reply.

## 5. Where `news` exists

| Case | Supplier | News | Our argument without an ID today |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | sup:70250 | `news:20260309-03` advertises free machine capacity | `their_capacity`, after it writes "we have free capacity" (24 replies in 8 sessions) |
| P05 | sup:70240 | `news:20260710-18` fully booked into next year | - |
| P10 | sup:70410 | `news:20260822-23` allocates volumes | - |
| P11 | sup:70140 | `news:20260911-28` restructures with its banks | - |
| P04 | sup:70620 | `news:20260619-15` concentrates on larger accounts | - |
| D02 | - | `news:N-0412` (in the case's refs) | - |

Only P05's free-capacity item argues for a lower price; it is the one case in the hosted set where the type could
be cited to our advantage, and D02 is where it can be tried without quota.

## 6. Measured after the audit

`tactical+news` on sandbox D02 (`runs.md` S-37 to S-40, [record](benchmarks/2026-10-11-tactical-news-none.md)): the
arena reads the type `news`; cited to the bidder it is about it is `verified` and "taken into account" (D02 0.587 →
0.713, four of four runs), cited to the other bidder it is `irrelevant`. Not played on practice.

content.content:
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.


## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |

| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |

once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

import json, sys, glob, math
S = sys.argv[1]
seen = {}
for p in glob.glob(f"{S}/rep/P02-*.json"):
    r = json.load(open(p))["result"]
    if not r.get("deal"): continue
    t = r["terms"]; b = r["cost_breakdown"]
    k = (t["unit_price"], t["payment_days"], (t["index_clause"] or {}).get("deadband_pct"))
    seen[k] = (b["relationship"], r["c_deal"], r["score"])
def soft(g): return 0 if g <= 0 else (g*g/10 if g <= 5 else g-2.5)
def inv(c):  # charge -> gap
    s = c/31920
    return 0 if s == 0 else (math.sqrt(10*s) if s <= 2.5 else s+2.5)
print("price pay db  charge  C  score  gap  => worth/F")
for k, (rel, c, sc) in sorted(seen.items()):
    g = inv(rel); m = 0.5 - g  # margin pct
    ratio = 1/(1-m/100) if rel > 0 else None   # worth/F
    print(k, round(rel), round(c), round(sc,3), round(g,3), ratio and round(ratio,5), ratio and round(k[0]/ratio,3))
EOF
uv run python $S/p02fit.py $S

######## correspondence/20251026-70140-N.md
# Holiday shutdown

email - 2025-10-26 - Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o.

Our plant is closed from 23 December to 6 January. Please place call-offs for January by 10 December.
######## correspondence/20260710-70140-M2.md
# Payment of invoices

email - 2026-07-10 - Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o.

Could you pay our invoices within 10 days? In return we would grant a cash discount.
######## correspondence/20260715-70140-M1.md
# Liquidity

call note - 2026-07-15 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Call with the managing director of Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o.: he asked twice whether we could pay earlier and said the bank is watching every month. 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.'
######## correspondence/20260921-70140-P11.md
# Escalation: delivery and quality performance

letter - 2026-09-21 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Supplier Quality

To Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o.

your rolling 12-month scorecard (sc:70140@2026Q3) is **red**: on-time delivery 63.5 %, 2376 ppm, 0 overdue 8D reports. We expect a binding improvement plan for Bearing bracket HN (part:310020) and will discuss quality commitments and cost recovery.

Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Supplier Quality
######## correspondence/20251225-70710-N.md
# Holiday shutdown

email - 2025-12-25 - Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Our plant is closed from 23 December to 6 January. Please place call-offs for January by 10 December.
######## correspondence/20260421-70710-M2.md
# Price discussion

call note - 2026-04-21 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Call with the owner of Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH: he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.
######## correspondence/20260706-70710-M1.md
# Material costs

letter - 2026-07-06 - Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear Sir or Madam,

for your information: our nickel and alloys requirement is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. Market movements reach our costs only after that.

Yours faithfully,
Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH
######## correspondence/20260912-70710-P08.md
# Price basis and surcharge clause for the coming period

letter - 2026-09-12 - Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear Sir or Madam,

for Round bar 1.4404 dia 30 mm, peeled (part:370010) we propose to agree the price basis for the coming period, including a price adjustment clause based on AS-14404. Please let us know your view.

Yours faithfully,
Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH
######## correspondence/20251019-70510-N.md
# Holiday shutdown

email - 2025-10-19 - Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

Our plant is closed from 23 December to 6 January. Please place call-offs for January by 10 December.
######## correspondence/20260227-70510-M2.md
# Annual review

meeting note - 2026-02-27 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Annual review with Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG. Their key account manager explained that price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
######## correspondence/20260410-70510-M1.md
# Annual review

meeting note - 2026-04-10 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Annual review with Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG. Their key account manager explained that price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
######## correspondence/20260914-70510-P02.md
# Price adjustment from 01 January 2027

letter - 2026-09-14 - Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

Dear Sir or Madam,

we have supplied Hollerau Pumpenwerke reliably for many years. Owing to the strong rise in copper and electronic component prices, we are forced to adjust our prices for Motor IE3 7.5 kW, 4-pole (part:350011) by **6.5 %** with effect from **01 January 2027**: from EUR 348.32 to EUR 370.96 per  pc.

We regret this step and ask for your understanding.

Yours faithfully,
Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

Between Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH and Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o..

**§ 5.1** Delivery FCA; standard lead time 56 days from order.

**§ 6.1** The quality agreement applies: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint.

**§ 8.1** Valid from 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30; extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice.

Between Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH and Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH.

FLAGS: dict[str, str] = {
    "alt_structure": "its alternative's structure goes into our next menu; its price only on an end signal or at "

    "persistent": "longer and steadier: our floor estimate ends nothing until two rounds are left, our steps are "

    "answers": "plain answers: the volume we need, an opener that matches its move, a fixed field said once, a "
